title: A Virtual Environment for One Project
description: Four commands that create a virtual environment, activate it, install a package into it, and check that the install worked.

steps.description: These four commands set up and test a virtual environment. A virtual environment gives one project its own Python and its own packages, so installing something for one lab cannot break another. It is a folder, usually named `.venv`.
`python3 -m venv .venv` creates the environment folder, `.venv`, in the current directory.
`source .venv/bin/activate` turns the environment on for this terminal. On Windows the command is `.venv\Scripts\activate`.
`python3 -m pip install requests` installs the `requests` package into the active environment, not into the system Python.
The `-c` one-liner imports `requests` and prints `requests ok`, a quick check that the package is importable.
